mainTopic: How the מצורע's shaving overrides the prohibitions of a נזיר and a כהן, and the rules for removing body hair with a razor
overview: The גמרא looks at the verse about a מצורע shaving "ראשו" (his head) and "זקנו" (his beard), and asks what each word teaches. First it challenges the view that an עשה does not override a לא תעשה ועשה: why not learn from a כהן מצורע, who must shave? The answer is that we cannot learn from a כהן, because his prohibition does not apply to everyone. For the other view, a ברייתא shows that "זקנו" teaches that a כהן מצורע must shave his beard with a razor. Another ברייתא proves that the beard prohibition covers only a razor. Then the גמרא explains that both words are needed, one for the נזיר and one for the כהן, because neither case can be learned from the other, and neither can serve as a source for other laws. Finally the topic turns to removing body hair. רב permits it with something like a razor, a ברייתא gives lashes for removing armpit or pubic hair with a real razor, and the גמרא concludes those lashes are only מדרבנן.

steps.title: Why not learn from the leprous priest?
steps.stepSummary: According to the view that an עשה does not override a לא תעשה ועשה, the גמרא challenges: just learn from a כהן מצורע, where the מצוה to shave does override.
steps.simpleTranslation: [According to the one who holds] that a positive מצוה does not come and override a prohibition together with a positive מצוה, let him learn from a כהן that it does override!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges one opinion. It points to the case of a כהן who is a מצורע, where the shaving מצוה does push aside his prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן is forbidden to shave the corners of his beard, yet a כהן מצורע must shave. So here an עשה does override a לא תעשה ועשה. Why doesn't this view learn the general rule from that case, instead of holding that an עשה does not override a לא תעשה ועשה?

keyTerms.meaning: A positive מצוה, something the Torah says to do
A prohibition, something the Torah says not to do
Pushes aside, overrides
Let him learn, let him derive

steps.confusionAlert: This step starts in the middle of a sentence. The opening words, which say whose opinion this is, come just before this text.

phrases.english: that a positive מצוה does not come
phrases.notes: This continues a sentence that started earlier. It means "according to the one who holds that..."

phrases.english: and override a prohibition and a positive מצוה,
let him learn from a priest, that it does override!
phrases.notes: He means a כהן who is a מצורע and must shave his beard even though a כהן normally may not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the challenge in this section, continuing the discussion of how "ראשו" is used.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that an עשה does not override a לא תעשה ועשה, and so needs a verse for the נזיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The כהן מצורע case shows an עשה overriding a לא תעשה ועשה, so this view should learn from it.

steps.title: A priest's prohibition is not for everyone
steps.stepSummary: We cannot learn from a כהן, because his prohibition does not apply to all Jews. For the same reason, a נזיר cannot be learned from a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we do not learn from a כהן: what is special about a כהן is that his is a prohibition that does not apply equally to everyone. A נזיר also cannot be learned from a כהן, since the כהן's prohibition does not apply equally to everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the כהן case is too special to learn from. So the נזיר still needs its own verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prohibition on a כהן shaving his beard applies only to כהנים, not to every Jew. A prohibition that is not for everyone may be weaker and easier to override. So we cannot use it as a model for general rules or for a נזיר, and "ראשו" is still needed to teach that the מצורע's shaving overrides the נזיר.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not learn from it, we do not derive from it
What is special about... that it... (a way of showing a case is different)
A prohibition that does not apply equally to everyone
A nazirite, a person who took a vow not to cut his hair, among other things

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key rule: a prohibition that applies only to some people cannot be the model for a prohibition that applies to anyone, like נזירות.

phrases.english: Rather, we do not learn from a priest:
what is special about a priest is that
it is a prohibition that is not equal for all.
phrases.notes: Only כהנים are forbidden to shave their beard corners. Regular Jews are not included in this prohibition.

phrases.english: A nazirite also cannot be learned from a priest,
since it is a prohibition that is not equal for all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 1 by showing the כהן case cannot be used as a model.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: the source case has a special feature the other cases lack
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We could learn the general rule, and the נזיר case, from the כהן מצורע.
steps.terutzMaskana: A כהן's prohibition is not for everyone, so nothing can be learned from it. "ראשו" is still needed for the נזיר.

steps.title: Then why does the verse say "his beard"?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the view that uses "ראשו" for the נזיר and asks what the extra word "זקנו" teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who applies this word "ראשו" to a נזיר, why do I need "זקנו"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks about the other view. It wants to know why the verse needs the word "זקנו" as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse already says the מצורע shaves "all his hair." If "ראשו" is used to teach about the נזיר, the word "זקנו" seems to add nothing. The גמרא expects every word in the verse to teach something.

keyTerms.meaning: Applies, sets the verse to refer to
His head (a word in the verse about the מצורע shaving)
His beard
Why do I need it? (asking what a word teaches)

phrases.english: And the one who applies this "his head" to a nazirite,
phrases.notes: The verse is ויקרא 14:9, where the מצורע shaves his head and his beard.

phrases.english: why do I need "his beard"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן דְּמוֹקֵים לְהַאי ״רֹאשׁוֹ״ בְּנָזִיר, לְמָה לִי ״זְקָנוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first view to the other view, and asks about a different word in the same verse.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word "זקנו" according to the view that uses "ראשו" for the נזיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Once "ראשו" teaches about the נזיר and the verse already includes all his hair, "זקנו" seems to have no job.

steps.title: "His beard" teaches about a leprous priest
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that "זקנו" teaches that a כהן מצורע must shave his beard, even though כהנים are normally forbidden to shave their beard corners.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for what is taught in a ברייתא: Why does the verse say "זקנו"? Since it says "they shall not shave the corners of their beard," I might think that even a כהן מצורע is the same. So the verse says "זקנו."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. "זקנו" teaches that a כהן who is a מצורע must still shave his beard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without "זקנו", we might think a כהן מצורע keeps his prohibition and does not shave his beard. The word "זקנו" tells us the מצורע shaving applies to him too. Why not learn the כהן from the נזיר? The גמרא explains later that נזירות can be undone by שאלה, so the כהן needs his own word.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it for (a different teaching)
The verse teaches, the verse says (to show us something)
I might have thought
A person with צרעת who must shave as part of becoming pure

steps.whatToRemember: Each word has its own job. "ראשו" teaches that the מצורע's shaving overrides the נזיר, and "זקנו" teaches that it overrides the כהן's beard prohibition. We cannot learn one from the other: the נזיר can't be learned from the כהן, whose prohibition is not for everyone, and the כהן can't be learned from the נזיר, because נזירות can be undone by שאלה.

phrases.english: He needs it for that which is taught:
"His beard" — why does the verse say it?
Since it is said
"and they shall not shave the corners of their beard,"
I might think even a leprous priest is the same,
phrases.notes: He means the כהן מצורע would also be forbidden to shave his beard.

phrases.english: so the verse says: "his beard."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 3 by giving "זקנו" its own job, based on a ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Giving the word a different purpose, supported by a ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "זקנו" seems extra once "ראשו" is used for the נזיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: "זקנו" is needed to teach that a כהן מצורע shaves his beard despite the כהן's prohibition.

steps.title: How do we know the מצורע shaves with a razor?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that the מצורע's shaving is done with a razor.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that this is talking about a razor?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to set up the next move: how do we know the shaving at issue is done with a razor? The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 said "זקנו" teaches that a כהן מצורע shaves his beard even though כהנים may not shave it. Now the גמרא asks how we know the מצורע's shaving is done with a razor. The next step answers by showing that the beard prohibition covers only a razor. If the תורה needed "זקנו" to permit his shaving, that shaving must be with a razor.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know this?
A razor

phrases.english: And from where do we derive that it is with a razor?
phrases.notes: He means: how do we know the מצורע's shaving has to be done with a razor?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the background fact needed to make the ברייתא in step 4 work: the clash only exists if the prohibition is about a razor.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that the מצורע's shaving is done with a razor.

steps.title: A ברייתא proves the beard prohibition is only with a razor
steps.stepSummary: Two פסוקים are combined: "לא יגלחו" (shaving) and "לא תשחית" (destroying). Only something that both shaves and destroys is forbidden, and that is a razor.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: "They shall not shave the corners of their beard." You might think that cutting with scissors is also forbidden, so the פסוק says "do not destroy." If the rule is only "do not destroy," you might think tweezers or a plane are forbidden too, so the פסוק says "shave." What kind of shaving also destroys the hair? A razor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. Combining two פסוקים shows that the prohibition is only shaving with a razor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "לא יגלחו" alone might include scissors, and "לא תשחית" alone might include tweezers or a plane. Putting them together means only a tool that both shaves and destroys the hair from the root is forbidden, and that is a razor. Since the תורה needed "זקנו" to permit the כהן מצורע to shave his beard, his shaving must be the forbidden kind, with a razor.

keyTerms.meaning: The corners of their beard
Scissors
Destroying the hair down to the root
Tweezers, a tool for plucking hairs
A carpenter's plane, a scraping tool

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean beard hair may be removed in any other way at all. The ברייתא only defines what this specific prohibition covers, which is a razor and not scissors, tweezers or a plane.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the classic source that the prohibition of shaving the corners of the beard applies only to a razor.

phrases.english: As it is taught: "And the corners of their beard they shall not shave,"

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל אַף גִּילְּחוֹ בְּמִסְפָּרַיִם יְהֵא חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: one might think that even if he cut it with scissors he would be liable,
so the verse teaches: "And you shall not destroy."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:27. Scissors cut the hair but don't destroy it down to the root.

phrases.english: If it is only "you shall not destroy,"
one might think that if he removed them with tweezers or with a plane he is liable —
so the verse teaches: "And the corners of their beard they shall not shave."
Which shaving involves destroying?
You must say: this is a razor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 5's question with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Combining "לא יגלחו" with "לא תשחית" shows that only a razor, which both shaves and destroys, is forbidden. Since "זקנו" was needed to permit the כהן מצורע's shaving, that shaving must be with a razor.

steps.title: Why does the פסוק need both "ראשו" and "זקנו"?
steps.stepSummary: According to the view that "ראשו" teaches that an עשה overrides a plain לאו, why write "ראשו" at all? "זקנו" already teaches that it overrides even a לא תעשה ועשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who uses "ראשו" to teach about a plain prohibition, why do I need the פסוק to write "ראשו," and why do I need it to write "זקנו"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the view that "ראשו" teaches that the מצורע's shaving overrides a plain לאו. If so, why are both words needed?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This view uses "ראשו" to teach that the מצורע's shaving overrides a plain לאו, one with no עשה attached. But "זקנו" already teaches that it overrides a לא תעשה ועשה, which is the harder case. If an עשה overrides something that strong, it should obviously override a plain לאו, so the גמרא asks why the פסוק needs both words.

keyTerms.meaning: A plain prohibition on its own, with no עשה attached
Why do I need it? (asking why something seems unnecessary)
To write

phrases.english: And the one who uses this word "his head"
for a plain prohibition alone,
phrases.notes: He means: to teach that the מצורע's shaving overrides a plain לאו, one with no עשה attached.

phrases.english: why do I need it to write "his head,"
and why do I need it to write "his beard"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן דְּמַפֵּיק לֵיהּ לְהַאי ״רֹאשׁוֹ״ לְלָאו גְּרֵידָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that "זקנו" is shown to override a real לא תעשה ועשה, the גמרא asks whether "ראשו" is extra.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that "ראשו" teaches that an עשה overrides a plain לאו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If "זקנו" teaches overriding the stronger לא תעשה ועשה, overriding a weaker plain לאו follows automatically, so one of the words seems extra.

steps.title: Each word could be read either way, so both are written
steps.stepSummary: Either word on its own could mean overriding a plain לאו or overriding a לא תעשה ועשה. Since both readings are equally possible, both words are written: one for the נזיר and one for the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It could mean overriding just a plain prohibition, and it could mean overriding a prohibition together with a positive command. Therefore it is evenly balanced, and both words come.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a single word would be unclear, so the תורה wrote both words to cover both cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Either word on its own could be read as overriding a plain לאו or as overriding a לא תעשה ועשה, and neither reading is stronger. The פסוק speaks generally, so it covers both the נזיר and the כהן, and each of them has a לא תעשה ועשה. So both words are put to use: one teaches about the נזיר and the other about the כהן. The next step explains why one of these cases cannot be learned from the other.

keyTerms.meaning: It could mean, it can be understood as
To push aside, to override
Evenly balanced, with neither side stronger
So let both of them come (both are needed)

steps.whatToRemember: According to this view, "ראשו" and "זקנו" are both needed. One word teaches that the מצורע's shaving overrides the נזיר's prohibition, and the other teaches that it overrides the כהן's prohibition. Both are cases of לא תעשה ועשה, and neither can be learned from the other.

phrases.english: It could mean overriding a plain prohibition alone,
and it could mean overriding a prohibition together with a positive command.
Therefore it is evenly balanced,
and let both of them come.
phrases.notes: Both words are needed, one teaching about the נזיר and the other about the כהן.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַשְׁמַע לְמִידְחֵי לָאו גְּרֵידָא, וּמַשְׁמַע לְמִידְחֵי לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה וַעֲשֵׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7's challenge by showing that neither word is extra.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Ambiguity resolution: one word alone would be unclear, so two words are needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "זקנו" alone teaches the stronger case, so "ראשו" is extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: A single word could be read as either case with equal force, so both words are written to teach both cases clearly.

steps.title: Why the נזיר and the כהן can't be learned from each other
steps.stepSummary: The law for a כהן can't come from a נזיר, because נזירות can be undone by asking a חכם. The law for a נזיר can't come from a כהן, because the כהן's prohibition doesn't apply to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: A כהן can't be learned from a נזיר, because a נזיר's vow can be undone by request. A נזיר can't be learned from a כהן, because the כהן's prohibition is not the same for everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer from Step 8. It explains why the תורה had to write both words, ראשו and זקנו, instead of letting us learn one case from the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case has a 'weak spot' that might make it easier to override. A נזיר's prohibition is weaker because the whole vow can be cancelled through שאלה. A כהן's prohibition is weaker because it applies only to כהנים, not to all Jews. So neither case can teach the other.

keyTerms.meaning: learns or derives one law from another
can be undone by asking a חכם to cancel the vow
a prohibition that does not apply to everyone

phrases.english: A priest cannot be learned from a nazirite,
since it can be undone by request.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the נזיר's vow, which a חכם can cancel.

phrases.english: A nazirite cannot be learned from a priest,
since it is a prohibition that is not equal for all.
phrases.notes: Only כהנים have this ban on shaving. Regular Jews don't have it.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּהֵן מִנָּזִיר לָא יָלֵיף, שֶׁכֵּן יֶשְׁנוֹ בִּשְׁאֵלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the תירוץ of Step 8 by explaining why one case can't be learned from the other.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each case has its own weak point, so both פסוקים are needed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One word should be enough, and the other case could be learned from it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each case can be challenged, so both ראשו and זקנו are necessary.

steps.title: These two cases can't serve as a general source
steps.stepSummary: In general, we can't learn from the נזיר and the כהן that an עשה overrides a לא תעשה ועשה, because each case has its weakness.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in general we don't learn from them, because they can be challenged, as we said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a wider conclusion. These two cases cannot be used as a source for other laws.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might want to say: since an עשה overrides a לא תעשה ועשה for both the נזיר and the כהן, it should do so everywhere. The גמרא rejects this. Each case has a special weakness, which is the שאלה for the נזיר and the 'not for everyone' prohibition for the כהן. So the rule stays limited to these two cases.

keyTerms.meaning: in general, in other cases
to challenge or refute a derivation
as we said earlier

steps.whatToRemember: An עשה overrides a לא תעשה ועשה only in these two cases, the נזיר and the כהן מצורע. We can't extend it to other laws, because each case has a weak point.
steps.whyThisMatters: This limits a powerful rule. Normally an עשה does not override a לאו that also comes with an עשה.

phrases.english: And in general we do not learn from them,
phrases.notes: He means we can't learn from these cases that an עשה overrides a לא תעשה ועשה in other laws.

phrases.english: because it can be refuted, as we said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the weak points from Step 9 to block a general derivation.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The rule that an עשה overrides a לא תעשה ועשה stays limited to the נזיר and the כהן מצורע.

steps.title: רב allows removing body hair with a razor
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that a person may remove all the hair of his body with a razor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: A person may lighten his whole body with a razor.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב says a person may remove his body hair with a razor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Lighten' means taking away the hair that weighs on him or bothers him. This is a regular person, not a נזיר. The beard and the corners of the head are separate prohibitions and are not part of this ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: lightens, removes hair to feel lighter
razor
his body

phrases.english: Rav said:
A person may lighten all his body with a razor.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: מֵיקֵל אָדָם כׇּל גּוּפוֹ בְּתַעַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic connected to the theme of shaving and razors.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person may remove the hair of his body with a razor.

steps.title: A ברייתא says removing armpit or pubic hair gets lashes
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that someone who removes armpit or pubic hair is flogged. This seems to contradict רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: One who removes the hair of the armpit or the pubic area gets lashes!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב with a ברייתא. The ברייתא says removing this hair is punished with lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב allowed removing 'all his body' hair, and that would include these places. The ברייתא treats removing exactly this hair as a punishable act. So the two sources seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: one who removes, here meaning hair
the armpit
gets lashes

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
One who removes the hair of the armpit and the pubic area
is flogged!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: הַמַּעֲבִיר בֵּית הַשֶּׁחִי וּבֵית הָעֶרְוָה
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that a person may remove all his body hair.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא punishes removing some of that same body hair with lashes.

steps.title: Razor versus scissors
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is talking about using a razor. רב is talking about using scissors.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one is with a razor, and that one is with scissors.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by saying the two sources are talking about different tools.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא punishes someone who uses a real razor. רב permits someone who uses scissors. With this split, the contradiction disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: scissors
this case ... that case, splitting two sources

phrases.english: This one is with a razor,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the ברייתא that gives lashes.

phrases.english: that one is with scissors.
phrases.notes: 'That one' is רב's ruling that allows it.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by the tool used.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב and the ברייתא are talking about the same act.
steps.terutzMaskana: Using a razor is punished, and using scissors is allowed.

steps.title: But רב said 'with a razor'
steps.stepSummary: The answer doesn't fit רב's words, because רב clearly said a razor.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב also said 'with a razor'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own answer. רב's own words mention a razor, not scissors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in Step 13 claimed that רב was talking about scissors. But the word בְּתַעַר is right there in רב's statement. So that split seems impossible.

steps.title: רב meant 'like a razor'
steps.stepSummary: רב meant scissors that cut close like a razor, not an actual razor.
steps.simpleTranslation: He meant something similar to a razor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads רב's words more carefully. 'With a razor' means a tool that works like a razor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב was describing scissors that cut very close to the skin, almost like a razor. So רב still allows only scissors, and the answer from Step 13 holds. A real razor remains forbidden, as the ברייתא says.

keyTerms.meaning: similar to, like

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read רב as permitting an actual razor. After this answer, רב permits only scissors that cut close like a razor.
steps.whatToRemember: Removing armpit or pubic hair with a real razor is punished. Close-cutting scissors are allowed.

phrases.english: Similar to a razor.

steps.terutzMaskana: רב meant scissors that cut close like a razor.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says removing armpit or pubic hair gets lashes
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא quotes רבי יוחנן: one who removes armpit or pubic hair is flogged.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: One who removes the hair of the armpit and the pubic area gets lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement is brought. רבי יוחנן rules that removing this hair is punished with lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches the ברייתא from Step 12. It is stated here as an אמורא's ruling, which sets up the next challenge about what kind of lashes he means.

steps.title: Removing hair is only a rabbinic prohibition
steps.stepSummary: A source says hair removal is forbidden only by the Rabbis, so why would there be lashes?
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: Removing hair is not forbidden by the Torah, only by the Rabbis!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן. A source says this hair removal is only a rabbinic law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה's 39 lashes are given only for breaking a תורה prohibition. If removing hair is only דברי סופרים, תורה lashes should not apply. So רבי יוחנן's 'is flogged' seems wrong.

steps.title: He means rabbinic lashes
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן meant lashes given by the Rabbis, not Torah lashes.

steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי יוחנן's word 'flogged'. He meant rabbinic lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Rabbis can give lashes for disobeying their decrees. This is called מכת מרדות. So רבי יוחנן agrees that the prohibition is only rabbinic, and the punishment is rabbinic too.
